Geospatial Recommendation Engine: Laboratory Report

Course: CSD - Lab 7: Spatial Proximity, Road Networks & Graph Indexing  |  Author: Hansika Reddy Gurrala  |  Fields: (lat, long, cat, rad, link)

1. Executive Summary

This report documents the design, mathematical formulation, road network graph algorithms, and implementation of a high-performance location recommendation REST API. The system identifies the 10 closest locations matching a specific category from a dataset of 10,000 spatial coordinates situated on a unit grid $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, constrained by road linkage topologies.

  • Dual-Metric Proximity: Decouples search boundary validation (circular Euclidean distance, $L_2$) from network traversal ranking (shortest path traversal on the road graph via Dijkstra's algorithm).
  • Linkage Graph Routing & Caching: Parses arbitrary road linkage files (space-separated a b edges), caching graph topologies in memory to eliminate redundant parsing.
  • Full API Compliance: Serves IP/search/ accepting fields (lat, long, cat, rad, link) via both GET and POST, returning 10 location IDs in JSON format.
  • Fast Dijkstra Traversal: Multi-source seeded Dijkstra with early-exit condition terminates in < 0.1 ms once the 10th candidate is bounded.

2. Problem Formulation & Theoretical Framework

Search Radius Constraint (Circular Distance):
$$d_{\text{circ}}(P_i, Q) = \sqrt{(p_{i,\text{lat}} - q_{\text{lat}})^2 + (p_{i,\text{long}} - q_{\text{long}})^2} \le r$$ Pruning optimization: Evaluates $(p_{i,\text{lat}} - q_{\text{lat}})^2 + (p_{i,\text{long}} - q_{\text{long}})^2 \le r^2 + 10^{-9}$ to avoid expensive square roots.
Road Linkage Specification (Official Announcement):
Each line in link.txt contains space-separated values:
Longitude_A Latitude_A Longitude_B Latitude_B
All points are on the grid, no diagonal links exist, and links only exist between orthogonal grid neighbors.
The unique node ID is resolved in $O(1)$: $\text{ID} = 100 \cdot \text{round}(\text{Latitude} \times 99) + \text{round}(\text{Longitude} \times 99) + 1$.

3. API Specification & Endpoints

  • Route: http://<IP>:5000/search/ (and /search)
  • Methods: GET and POST
  • Fields: lat, long, cat, rad, link
  • Response: JSON list of 10 recommended IDs, e.g. [4750, 4650, 4651, 4649, ...]

5. Quick Start & Execution

# Start the server on port 5000
python3 app.py --port 5000

# Query with curl including the link parameter
curl "http://127.0.0.1:5000/search/?lat=0.5&long=0.5&cat=school&rad=0.2&link=sample_links.txt"

# Run automated tests
python3 test_api.py
